events.text: Something very small has lain down on you and sighed. You think it did so some time ago. You have been holding things up for so long that you have stopped noticing them one by one; there is the valley, the river, the weight of the hills. But that sigh has stayed with you for a year or two. You could send some of your attention up to it. It would take all of a summer to arrive.

choices.text: Send it up, slowly, through the clay

effects.log: It rises about the height of a person each month. Roots go past it, a lost spoon, an old well. In the autumn it comes up under a floor, and it stops, and it listens. So that is what it is like up here. It is very busy.

choices.text: No. Everything above you is a thing you are already holding

effects.log: You let your attention sink back. The sigh stops mattering after a decade or so. You hold up the valley, evenly. Nobody asks you to do anything else.

events.text: Your attention comes up under a big house, and you learn feet. There is no other way to learn anyone from below. A heavy one who stops at every door. A light one who runs and is told not to. One who walks softly past a certain room, every night, at the same hour. You know more about this family than its own ancestors do by the first snow. You have not yet worked out what any of them look like.

choices.text: Stay, and learn what the feet mean

effects.log: It takes eleven years to be sure of the one in the soft shoes. It was love, or else it was theft. By then they have all died or moved, and the feet are different. You note that this happens.

choices.text: Shift a little, and see if they notice

effects.log: A wall cracks by the width of a grain. The whole house stands around it talking, for a week, and in the end they blame the cat. You are rather shaken at how little it took.

events.text: Someone is digging. You find this out as one finds a fly on the ear. A spade comes down into a farmyard on a bad day, in a bad spot, for a new privy, and goes into you by about a hand. It tickles. Within the month the man with the spade is in bed with a grey face. Earth-sickness, says the shaman, and his household are out there with rice and apologies. You did nothing. You think you did nothing.

choices.text: Warm the ground under his mat, to see if it helps

effects.log: It takes a while to reach him. He gets up in the spring, thin and very polite, and he fills in the hole by himself. They go on using the old privy. You are pleased, and you are not sure what about.

choices.text: Lie still. If it was you, you should learn what you do

effects.log: You pay attention, for once. He does not get up. It may have been the water, or it may have been you. You keep that spade's depth in your memory, exactly, and nobody digs there again.

events.text: A bean comes through a crack in a floor. A small person dropped it and looked for it, and cried, and has long since grown up. It lies against you in the dark. It takes you about a season to understand what has happened: for the first time in as long as you can recall, you have been given something, by accident. You have borne the weight of kings, and you find that you cannot stop thinking about this bean.

choices.text: Keep it warm, and let it do as beans do

effects.log: It comes up through the yard one spring, where nothing has any right to grow. An old woman looks at it for a while, and leaves it, and ties it to a stick. There are beans in that yard for two hundred years.

choices.text: Keep it. It is yours

effects.log: You hold it very still. It never sprouts. It is still there, and it is the only thing you own, in a whole country that stands on you. You had not known that you wanted one.

events.text: {npc} rents the back room of a poor house at the edge of the valley, and {he} has a bad back, so {he} sleeps with no mat, flat on the floor. It is late. You have been under this room for some years now, not for any reason. {npc} puts {his} palm down on the boards beside {him}, and pats them twice, as one might a horse. "Whoever is down there," {he} says, "I paid for this month in advance. Hold still."

choices.text: Warm the one place under that palm

effects.log: You start at once. It gets there by the spring. {He} stops with {his} hand on the floor one night and looks at it for a long while. Then {he} moves the whole of {his} bedding over about one pace, without saying anything.

choices.text: Sink back down. People on floors are not your concern

effects.log: You go. It is no great journey; you only stop attending. {He} stays till {his} month is up, and for another nine years, and the back gets no better. It was a perfectly ordinary floor.

events.text: {npc} has started talking to the floor at night. It is only about the day: who owes for what, the price of salt, what a fool the landlord is. Now and then {he} asks something. "Will it rain, do you think?" You give the matter all your attention. You have an answer, quite a good one, ready in about four years. {He} has asked you a great many things since then. You are falling behind. You had never been behind before.

choices.text: Answer what you can: warm for yes, and cool for no

effects.log: It is three years late, and it is about some rain that has already fallen. {He} laughs out loud, alone, in the dark, when {he} works it out. {He} starts asking you things {he} can wait for.

choices.text: Hurry. Try to answer tonight's question tonight

effects.log: You have never hurried. The room jumps. Every bowl in the house jumps with it, and the dog goes under the step. "Well," says {npc}, from the floor, after a while. "Never mind about the rain."

events.text: There are little tremors in this valley, most years. {npc} has come to suspect something. You watch {him} do it, by the feet: {he} fills a bowl to the very lip, and sets it down in the middle of the room, and goes out to the road, and stands, and feels the ground shiver under {his} sandals. {He} comes back in and looks at the bowl. It has not spilled. It has not so much as ringed. {He} sits down in front of it.

choices.text: Let one ring go across it, gently, to say yes

effects.log: One small ring goes out from the middle, and it touches the rim and stops. {He} sits there through the whole of that night without touching it. In the morning {he} drinks the water, quite slowly.

choices.text: Keep it still. Let {him} be as sure as {he} likes

effects.log: It lies there like a plate. {He} nods at it, as one nods to a neighbour who will not gossip. You think that this may be the most anyone has ever understood you, and you did nothing at all.

events.text: It is the tenth month. Behind the soy jars there is a jar with a straw cap gone black, forgotten since the last tenants. {npc} has found it. {He} tips three years of dust and mouse over the wall, scrubs it, and fills it with new rice {he} cannot afford. {He} ties on a new cap with a very bad knot, and lays {his} palm on the ground beside it. "That is yours," {he} says. "I do not know your name."

choices.text: Come up under the jar, and warm it through

effects.log: It takes you all of the winter, and you have never done anything so fast. In spring, the rice in that jar is warm to the hand, and a few grains have started to grow. {He} ties the cap on again. It is still a very bad knot.

choices.text: Let the rice go sour. You have been fed by kingdoms

effects.log: It takes no effort at all. {He} lifts the cap at the new year, and looks, and smells it, and gives the whole jar to the neighbour's pig. {He} does not do it again. {He} still sleeps on the floor. It is only a floor.

events.text: The river has come over the dyke in the night, up to the eaves all down the lane. You cannot stop it; water does not listen to you. You can only hold. {npc} is on the roof with the jar in {his} arms, and you have the corner posts of that house gripped in the clay like teeth in a pear. Three houses down, a house quietly leaves. You could hold more thinly, and hold the lane.

choices.text: Hold this house. Only this one

effects.log: It stands up out of the brown water in the morning, the only one for a long way. They bring the neighbours there in boats. {npc} looks around at the whole of the lane, and {he} does not thank the floor that year.

choices.text: Spread it out under the whole lane

effects.log: You keep nine houses of the twelve. The back wall of {npc}'s goes down in the small hours, with the good pot. {He} shovels mud for a month, among neighbours, and {he} is singing some of the time.

events.text: You feel it nine days away. Far off under the sea something has slipped, and it is walking this way along the rock. It gets here at dinner time. Every pillar in the valley starts to walk. You grip. A crack runs over the yard, under the wall and across the floor, and stops a span from where {npc} sits with a spoon halfway to {his} mouth. {He} looks down. {He} eats the spoonful.

choices.text: Take the whole of it into yourself

effects.log: It goes into you and stays there, and for some years you ache in a place that you did not know you had. The valley loses a few chimneys. The jar has not moved. There is a very nice crack to step over.

choices.text: Let it go by, and pass it on down the valley

effects.log: It goes where it was going, with a little more on it, to a county that you have never given any thought to. Your own people are fine. Word comes in the spring, by the peddlers, and {npc} goes very quiet with {his} palm on the floor.

events.text: The trouble is that you cannot tell a knock from a stamp. You answer them all, as you have been shown to. A dropped spoon gets a warm patch, and a quarrel in the kitchen gets a long slow swell that leaves the door hanging open. A drunk uncle fell over at the new year, and the floor came up a little to meet the man, who has given up drinking. "Not everything," says {npc} to the boards, "is for you."

choices.text: Learn the difference. It may take you some years

effects.log: It takes you nineteen. In the end you can tell {his} palm from every other thing that has ever touched that floor. You answer only that. It seems a very small thing to know, and you would not give it up for a province.

choices.text: Go on answering. You like to be polite

effects.log: They get a name in the district as a house that is listened to. People come by with small problems and stand around on the floor. {npc} has to put up a bench, and {he} blames you, at length, and you do not get to that for a while.

events.text: They need a well. The old one has gone salt, and it is a long walk now, and the shoulder that {npc} carries with is bad. The man has come with sticks to choose the spot, and has chosen it: right there, in the middle of the yard, where the ground is so oddly warm. Nobody may dig there. No one ever said so, or knows it, but you. The man is coming back with spades in three days.

choices.text: Make the spades ring on stone, every time

effects.log: They try it in six places, swearing. It is rock, they say, right under the dirt, the whole yard. They go away with their money. {npc} goes on walking to the far well, and the shoulder gets worse. You are holding that up as well.

choices.text: Under {his} palm that night, let the whole floor breathe, once

effects.log: It takes all night to rise by the width of a grain, and all of the next day to sink. {He} lies through it with {his} eyes open. Then {he} goes out and sends away the diggers and pays them for the trouble, and {he} does not say why. {He} knows now.

choices.text: Let them dig. Let them reach you, and see

effects.log: At twice a man's height the spade comes up yellow, and steaming. The diggers are over the wall before it has stopped ringing. {npc} stands at the top and looks down for a long while. It is filled in by nightfall, and the shaman is sent for, and everybody is a little ill.

events.text: There is a cart in the yard. You know that by the wheels. {npc} has a brother with land three provinces off, the salt tax has gone up, and this house was only ever rented. It is all quite reasonable. {He} lies flat on the floor the last night, with {his} palm on the boards. "Come on, then," {he} says, very quietly. {He} knows. You have held up the valley since the hills were new, and you have no feet.

choices.text: Hold still. Let {him} go

effects.log: The wheels go up the road for about a morning, and you can feel them for some way. You keep that floor warm, year after year. Other people come and go on it. They say that it is a good floor, and you hold it up.

choices.text: Let the road go soft, as far as the ford, for a month

effects.log: The axle sinks to the hub, three times. Everyone says that they have never seen the like, in a dry month. {He} walks back and stands in the door and looks at the floor, and {he} does not sit down. It is the smallest thing you ever did, and the worst.

choices.text: Push up a fistful of yourself, through the crack, under {his} hand

effects.log: It is warm yellow clay. It is as far as you can go. {He} holds it till morning. It is not you, and {he} knows that, and so do you. Then {he} ties it up in a cloth, and goes out to the cart and starts to take things off it, and {he} does not explain to anyone.

events.text: There has been a child on that floor. {bk_child}, born in the middle of the room, because there was no time for anywhere else. You felt it, as you feel most things, somewhat later; it weighs nothing at all. The midwife is washing the hands. The midwife goes on washing them, calls for more water, and holds one up to the lamp. There is a fine yellow dust in the creases. {npc} looks at it, and pats the floor twice.

choices.text: Warm the place where it lies

effects.log: It stops crying at once, and the midwife gives up on the hands. There is now one more small weight in the world that you can tell from all others, and you would know it in the dark, from below, for ever.

choices.text: Do nothing. Do not make it anything but a child

effects.log: You lie very still, with a great effort. It cries in the ordinary way, all night, and {npc} walks up and down on you with it until dawn, and you learn those feet again. They are slower now, and more careful. You like them better.

events.text: {bk_child} is learning to walk, and you are the one being learned on. It is three steps and then the floor, and three steps and the floor, and you find you have started to come up a little to meet it, as you would a dropped egg. Not one bruise, in a whole year. At the door sill it stops and it howls, and it will not go over. {npc} carries it out to the yard, and it screams until it is set down on the ground.

choices.text: Let it be. A floor is a good thing to love

effects.log: {npc} gives up, and has the door left open. It plays on the sill, with one foot on the boards. You know that you ought to be worried about this, and you will get to that in a few years.

choices.text: Stop coming up to meet it. Let it fall

effects.log: It falls and it bumps its nose. It looks at the floor in astonishment. It takes a long time before you get over the sound, and by then it can walk across the yard and has stopped looking back.

events.text: {bk_child} is seven, has clean hands, and has just given a long account of a peddler's cart. There was a mule. There were twelve kinds of needle. {bk_child} asks where the road goes. To the ford, says {bk_love}. And after that? You have waited seven years to feel that small weight settle. It is up on its toes at the gate. It is an entirely ordinary child, and it cannot wait to go.

choices.text: Be glad. Someone in this house should see a mule

effects.log: You hold up the road as far as the ford for that child, later on, every step, as far as you are able. Then the feet go off the edge of what you can tell. You had thought that you would mind it more. No: you mind it just as much as you thought.

choices.text: Soften the road a little, in the wet months

effects.log: It does nothing, only mud. The child stays home that year and is very bored at you, and the year after goes anyway, with better boots. {bk_love} pats the floor, one time only, not gently.

events.text: The worst flood yet. You have every post of that house in your teeth, nine days now, and there is too much. You have never thought that before. {bk_love} is carrying things up to the roof. {bk_child}, who is seven, has not gone up, and has lain down flat on the floor, cheek to the boards, and patted it twice. And something comes off you. It is very small. It is exactly as heavy as a seven-year-old's back.

choices.text: Let it hold. Let the small one carry that much

effects.log: You have held up the world since it began, and no one has ever taken the other end. The water goes down on the eleventh day. {bk_child} sleeps for a week, with yellow in every crease. {bk_love} looks from the child to the floor, and neither is going anywhere. Someone else has the other end of it now.

choices.text: Take it back. Nobody that small should ever feel this

effects.log: You take the whole of it back, and you are not sure how. The roof goes, in the night, but the floor stays. {bk_child} sits up, furious, and pats the boards again, and you do not answer, and that goes on for years. It knows. Nothing you can do will make it not know.

events.text: Getting down to the floor has become a whole undertaking for {npc}. There is a stool involved, and some language, and then {he} is down, and {he} puts {his} palm on the boards, and getting up again will use up most of the morning. {He} still fills the jar. {His} knots are no better. "You could raise it a bit," {he} says to you. "A floor as old as you are. You could come up and meet a person halfway."

choices.text: Raise that one place, by the width of a grain each year

effects.log: You have never been asked for anything so hard. There is a low mound now in the middle of that room, polished, about as high as a stool. Everyone trips on it. {He} sits on it in the evenings, and {he} is unbearably smug.

choices.text: Stay level. Warm the floor instead, all year

effects.log: It is what you know how to do. {He} lies down in the end and stays down for most of the day, with {his} back quite easy, telling you the news. It is all late news. You have got used to that.

events.text: {bk_love} is laid out on that floor for three days, as is proper, in the middle of the room. You have known that weight for fifty years. You could have picked it out of a marching army. There is less of it than there was, and it has not moved, and you keep expecting that it will. On the third morning they lift it, and all the feet go out at the door, and up the hill. You cannot go up the hill.

choices.text: Hold. There is a floor to hold up

effects.log: You do. Somebody ties the jar's cap the next autumn, with a good, tight, neat knot. It is that knot which finally does it. It takes a while to reach you, and the whole valley settles by about the width of a grain.

choices.text: Send everything you have under the hill. It is three li

effects.log: Nothing in you has moved so far so quickly. It reaches the mound in nine years. The grass on it stays green in the snow, from then on, and people come to look. You lie under it, and the floor back there has gone cold, and that is what it costs.

events.text: A hundred years on, and they are still here. {bk_child}'s people have bought the house and the one next door, and have never gone anywhere they could avoid. They are large and calm and very good at waiting. A man came with a fine offer for the land last spring. They gave him soup. His offer has doubled, and they are having more soup. The jar is full. They think this is simply how it is done.

choices.text: Send them a good year, up through the floors

effects.log: Things drift towards them, as they do: a stray ox, a lost debt, somebody's rich and tired aunt. They take it all quite calmly. They are not especially grateful. You find that this is restful.

choices.text: Let them be. They do not need you to hold them up

effects.log: They are holding something up themselves, it seems, in a small way, and not one of them knows. You look at that for several decades. You had no idea that it was this pleasant to be leaned against.

events.text: The road has brought someone back, of {bk_child}'s line, three provinces and five generations from here. You know by how they stand, and how much they hate it. The old house has been a ruin for sixty years. They have come on foot with bad blisters and a small knotted cloth. They get down in the weeds, unwillingly, and untie it. It is a fistful of yellow clay. They push it back into the ground.

choices.text: Take it in. Warm the place all the way up

effects.log: It takes until the snow. They have built a hut by then and they do not intend to leave it. Their palm is on the ground most evenings, patting it twice. Nobody ever told them to do that.

choices.text: Lie quiet. It is only clay, and they should go home

effects.log: They wait for three days. They bow to the weeds in an embarrassed way, and they limp off. You feel them all the way to the ford, and you are still holding that little patch of ground, and it was never heavy before.

events.text: There is someone on your floor. You stopped attending to this one sixty years ago, when it was left empty. {npc} has come in out of the rain with a peddler's pack and made a fire on the bare boards, which is very rude. "I am only here till spring," {he} says aloud, to nobody. {He} has said that in nine counties. {He} is going to leave. It is the first thing you know about {him}, from how {he} stands.

choices.text: Warm the floor anyway. {He} should know what {he} is leaving

effects.log: It takes till the thaw. {He} puts {his} hand down one morning and leaves it there, and starts to swear in a low steady voice. {He} tells you {he} has heard about this sort of floor. The pack stays where it is. It does not get unpacked, not for years.

choices.text: Stay cold. Let {him} go at the thaw, as {he} said

effects.log: The feet go up the road on the first dry day, quite cheerful. You have had the practice. You hold the floor up, with the small burnt place in the middle of it.

events.text: Someone has come a very long way, and hated it. They reach the yard on foot, grey with the road, complaining of every step to no one. They sit down on the bare ground over you with a groan of real happiness, take off their shoes, and put both palms flat. There is yellow in the creases. "Do not get up," they say. "I only came to say that the floors are terrible everywhere else."

choices.text: Warm the ground under them, right through

effects.log: They fall asleep where they sit, in the middle of the day, with their mouth open. It is three days before they stir. They leave a bean. You did not expect that, and there is no way that they could have known.

choices.text: Give them one slow breath of ground, and let them go

effects.log: It lifts them by the width of a grain, and it sets them down. They laugh until they cough. Then they put on their shoes with a heavy sigh and go home, the whole way, on those feet.

events.text: The teacher has sent you home with a note about your hands. They are not clean. They have never been clean. There is a fine yellow dust in the creases that you have scrubbed with ash, sand and a bristle brush, and it stays, as if you had just been digging. {npc} reads the note, turns your hand over, and looks at it with no surprise at all. {He} goes on with what {he} was eating.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Ask {him} why it will not come out

effects.log: "It is not on your hands," says {npc}, chewing. You look at them for quite a long time, and you stop scrubbing. The teacher goes on sending notes. They make a very good fire.

choices.text: Keep your hands in your sleeves, from now on

effects.log: You get very neat at it. You do your sums with your fingers curled. Nobody has looked at your palms since then, and you take to shaking hands, later on, very quickly.

events.text: You are at the Cho house for the harvest meal, sitting on their floor, and you have stopped listening. There is something the matter with it, over by the storeroom. You mention this. You are small, and everybody laughs, and old Cho says that the grandfather laid it. "It is going to go, at that corner," you say. "It is sad about it." {npc} kicks you, without looking, under the low table.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Say which beam. Say how long it has

effects.log: The storeroom corner goes down two winters later, right on the beam you named, with a great deal of millet. After that, people ask you over a good deal more, and you are given the good cushion, and they watch you sit.

choices.text: Say that you were only playing

effects.log: They believe you. It goes down two winters later, and it takes the millet with it, and you help to shovel. You do not eat much that day. {npc} passes you more rice and says that you did right, in a voice that does not settle it.

events.text: The family is going to the market town for the festival, a day and a half by cart, and this is thought to be a treat. You are fine as far as the first ridge. At the second you are sick over the side. It is not the cart. Your teeth ache, your hands are cold, and you have a clear sense of having left something on, some pot, some door. {npc} looks at you, and at the road behind you, and {he} sighs and gets down.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Say that you have to go home. Walk back, by yourself

effects.log: It is only a day. It gets better with each step, until you are running. You spend that festival alone on the floor at home, with cold rice, perfectly happy. Nobody ever quite forgives you that.

choices.text: Grit your teeth, and go on to the town

effects.log: You see the lanterns, and the wrestlers, and you remember them only as a kind of fever. You eat nothing for three days. You have done it. You make sure that everyone knows you liked it very much.

events.text: Dano, in your sixteenth summer, and they push you into the wrestling for a joke. The big Cho boy gets your belt in both hands and heaves. Nothing happens. The boy looks puzzled, and heaves with the whole back, then two friends help, and the sand is creeping over your ankles. You feel only a slow enormous calm. {npc} walks you home. "Eat something," {he} says. "Then I will tell you what is under the house."
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Hear all of it

effects.log: A palm on a floor, and a jar with a bad knot; a child called {bk_line}, with yellow in the hands. And the one below: {bk_anc}. {npc} tells it in no hurry. You find you are in no hurry either. It may be some years before you have finished thinking about it.

choices.text: Say that the Cho boy was only tired

effects.log: "Tired, yes," says {npc}, and goes in. You sit on the step by yourself until it is dark. The step is warm. You get up and go to bed, and you take the mat that is highest off the floor.

events.text: You have never run after anything in your life, and you own four stray oxen. They came up the road and stopped. So did a debt someone else owed, a very good kettle, and last month a distant aunt. {npc} says that this is your whole inheritance: you stay where you are, and the world comes round, like water to a low place. {He} says it while looking at the aunt, with some alarm.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Keep the door open, and feed whoever comes

effects.log: You are feeding eleven by winter, and it never quite runs out. They all think that they found you by luck. You have become, it would seem, a place. The aunt has taken over the kitchen, and the aunt will outlive everyone.

choices.text: Walk the oxen back, and the kettle, to their owners

effects.log: It takes the whole summer, and you are ill for most of it. People are amazed at you, and they tell you so, with their oxen. It does not stop, but you have shown that you do not mean it.

events.text: The new magistrate wants the whole lane cleared for a granary. It is a very good plan. The magistrate's clerk has been round with the paper, and all the neighbours have gone, some with compensation. You have gone on sitting at home. Nobody has laid a hand on you. They come to the gate, look at you, go away, and come back with another paper. {npc} says that you could at least pretend to have heard.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Stay where you are, and go on staying

effects.log: The granary goes up around you on three sides, in the end, with a kink in its wall. It takes eleven years. You sell them your millet. The clerk retires, and comes by now and then to look at you, in a friendly way.

choices.text: Sign, and take the silver, and move two li up the road

effects.log: It is only two li. You lie awake for a month, feeling as if you had your shoes on the wrong feet. It is a good dry site, and the floor is very nice. You keep on going back, at night, to stand in a granary.

events.text: A wet summer, and you wake up knowing. By evening there are clouds over the far ridge, and nobody is worried yet. In the night the river comes up through the low end of the village and stops, very exactly, at your gatepost. By dawn you have forty people on your floor, with their pigs. {npc} hands out rice. They keep looking down at the boards, and then at you.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Open the back room too. Say that the house has always been like this

effects.log: They stay for nine weeks. They go home saying that you have the best floor in the province, and they say it in a low voice. There is a path worn to your gate now that nobody can account for.

choices.text: Say that it is high ground, and that it was only luck

effects.log: You go up on the roof and show them how the land lies, with a stick, and it is quite convincing. It is a little lower than the Baks', in fact. {npc} says nothing about that. The Baks did the sums, some time later on.

events.text: {npc} has a sister in the south, and in all these years you have never gone to see the sister. There has always been a reason: the harvest, your back, the dog. {He} no longer asks. Tonight {he} has stopped in the middle of the room with the lamp, looking at you on the floor, as you always are, and at the raised bed you bought for {him} and never use. "What is it?" {he} says. "Is it me?"
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Put {his} palm on the boards. Tell {him} what is under them

effects.log: You tell it badly, and slowly. {He} keeps {his} hand there long after you have finished, and {his} face changes. "All this time," {he} says. "You could have just said that you were married." {He} goes to see the sister alone, and comes back.

choices.text: Say that it is only your back. Say next year, for certain

effects.log: It is next year, and you are very sorry. {He} goes south alone, in the end. {He} writes. Something has moved, by the width of a grain, and it is the sort of thing that you would be the first to feel.

events.text: You come in to find {npc} asleep on the bare floor in the middle of the day, cheek on the boards, one hand flat, with a perfectly good mat a pace away. {He} has been offered a place in a very good school in the provincial town, by people who do not offer that lightly. {He} has said that {he} will go, of course. You turn over the small hand. You did not need to. There is yellow in the lines.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Let {him} stay. Tell {him} what {he} is, and what it will cost

effects.log: {He} takes it calmly, as your people do. You show {him} how to stand when somebody heaves. {He} writes the school a very courteous letter. Sooner or later that school will come to {him}. You do not say so. That part teaches itself.

choices.text: Pack {his} bag. Put {him} on the cart, sick or not

effects.log: {He} is sick at the second ridge, as you knew. You had told the driver not to stop. {He} writes very good letters from that school. They say nothing, carefully, and you read them on the floor.

events.text: {npc} deals in ground: good sites for rich men's houses, better ones for their tombs. {He} has stopped at your gate, running a long knotted cord through {his} fingers, and {he} takes a long time to measure your yard, your door and you. "I have a client," {he} says, "who would pay a year's rice to lie in the ground with someone like you. Bones are bones. I can wait. I notice you do not go anywhere."
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Pick {him} up, and put {him} outside the gate

ok.log: {He} gets no purchase on you at all. {He} lands in the road, and gets up, and carefully winds in the cord, and notes down something about your reach. {He} bows. You have met a great many people in a hurry, and {he} is not one.

fail.log: You do not move, and {he} has planned for that: {he} goes for the knees, with something short. You are carried in. {He} measures you as you lie there, very politely.

choices.text: Offer {him} some soup, and say nothing about anything

effects.log: {He} eats it, standing, looking at your floor. It is excellent soup. You talk about rain. {He} ties one more knot in the cord before {he} leaves, and you find you have been holding your breath, and you let it out slowly.

events.text: You go out to look at your fields, and the neighbours' are not the neighbours' any more. {npc} has bought them: the Bak land, the Cho orchard, the strip along the ditch. {He} sits on your step with the knotted cord, grey now, and seems pleased to see you. Nobody can move you, {he} agrees. But {he} owns the road, the ditch and the well, and {he} would like to dig. "Only at the corner," {he} says.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: End the matter. Here, in your own yard, on your own ground

ok.log: On this ground, nothing can get under you. It does not take long. {He} goes off down {his} own road, walking oddly, with the cord in {his} hand all in a tangle, and the deeds go into your stove. That is the only time you see {him} hurry.

fail.log: You had thought the ground would do it for you. {He} has already had a trench cut along your wall by night, for just this. It gives, and you go down with it. {He} stands over you with the cord. "There," {he} says. "That is what I wanted to know."

choices.text: Pay {him} for the well, and let {him} dig at the far corner

effects.log: {He} digs, and it is dirt, all the way down; you have made very sure. {He} looks into that hole for a long time. Then {he} takes your silver, and bows, and {he} never comes back. {He} has a very good memory. So have you. You will see which of you lasts.

choices.text: Go on sitting. You have waited out better

effects.log: It takes eleven more years. You drink from the ditch. You walk to market by the fields, and your feet are in nobody's way. {He} gets very old on your step, in the end, still courteous, and {he} has a cough, and you start to bring out a cushion.

events.text: Some afternoons a heaviness comes on you. You stop in the yard with the bucket in your hand. It would be so simple to lie down. Everything in the district has started to feel as though it were resting on you, and you would like to get under it properly. They found you yesterday at dusk, flat behind the soy jars, with the ants going round you. "It asks," says {npc}, helping you up. "But it is very slow."
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Lie down, for a whole week, and find out

effects.log: You do not eat. It is not at all unpleasant. Things go by, up there: rain, a dog, somebody calling. When you get up, it is a good deal later than you thought, and you know where every well in the county is.

choices.text: Sleep on a raised bed. Take a long trip every year

effects.log: You go as far as the coast, the next year, and you are ill the whole way, and you look at the sea, which has no floor at all, and you dislike it very much. It helps. You come back heavier than you left, by about what you would expect.

events.text: It is coming. You have known for nine days, and you have told nobody, because nobody believes that kind of thing about nine days. Something is walking this way along the rock, and it will get here about dinner time. You feel like someone standing under one end of a very long beam. Someone could hold this. You think you could hold about the width of one village. {npc} is looking at how you stand.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Stand in the middle of the yard, and hold it

effects.log: You stand for three nights. On the third it comes, and all the dogs cry, and your own lane loses one chimney. There is blood in your nose, and you cannot speak until the new moon. There are people who have started to bow to you, and they are not joking.

choices.text: Go from door to door, and get them all out to the fields

effects.log: They think that you are mad, and about half of them come. It takes the houses of the others. You spend the night in a field with a lot of angry people, and they are alive. You are sick for a month from sleeping away from the floor.

events.text: {npc} takes you there by a road you would never have chosen, and you are sick twice. It is not much of a place: a low mound with weeds on it, and a jar sunk to its lip. There has been no house for a very long time. Somebody has been filling the jar. {npc} says that it was not {him}. You kneel, lay your palm on the ground, pat it twice, and wait. {bk_anc} is in no hurry.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Stay until it answers, however long it takes

effects.log: It takes until the morning of the fourth day. {npc} brings food. Then the ground under your hand goes warm, and stays warm, and you understand that it has been answering a question that someone put to it four hundred years ago. It is yes.

choices.text: Fill the jar, and tie the cap, and go home

effects.log: You have brought new rice. You tie the knot with care, and it comes out very badly, for no reason, and you can't improve it. You leave it so. You are not sick on the way home, not even once, and {npc} remarks on that.

events.text: {npc} has brought you across three provinces to a bean field in the old capital. Big stones stand in rows among the beans, sixty or so. It was the greatest temple in the country, says {npc}. A king began a palace here, on this low wet ground, and something yellow was seen, and the king thought again. It burned long ago. A farmer goes by without looking. You take off your shoes. {bk_anc} is under here.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Stand on the middle stone, and let it have your weight

effects.log: You stand there until the farmer comes to ask you if you are all right. Nothing has happened. But you can feel exactly where you are, for the first time in your life, and it turns out that it is the middle of everything, wherever you are.

choices.text: Bow to the stones. Then help the farmer with the beans

effects.log: You do a whole row, until sundown. The farmer gives you some for the road. It seems a much better use of that ground than anything a king has ever thought of, and something very old and very heavy seems, you could swear, to agree.

events.text: You have not left the yard in three years, and you have only just noticed. There is grass in the path to your gate. {npc} sits down by you, which takes a while. "You are going into the ground by inches," {he} says, "and taking the rest of us with you." You could go to the far south, and stay. You could lie down here, and not get up. {He} has heard of one other way.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Get on the cart. Keep going till there is no yellow in your hands

effects.log: You are sick for a whole year, across four provinces. Then one morning you wake up in an inn, and it is only an inn, and the palms of your hands are clean. You look at them for a long time. You order breakfast.

choices.text: Lie down in the yard, and stop getting up

effects.log: It is a great relief. People come to you now, and they bring things. You answer questions in your own time. The grass has grown over your feet, and nobody could say how long it would take to get you out of there, or that they should try.

choices.text: Take a fistful of the clay in a cloth, and go, and come back at the tenth month

effects.log: Nobody has done this, and it makes you ill. You go where you are needed, with the cloth around your neck, for as long as you can bear to. Each tenth month you come home and fill the jar. {npc} says that it is the first new thing anyone in your line has done in a thousand years.

events.text: You have lived in nine towns. You are very bad at it, and you love it. You have a favourite noodle stall you will never see again, and you can sleep on a raised bed and even in a boat. {npc} has tracked you down with news from home, and you nod, looking out of the window. The floor of this inn is uneven. It is only a floor. You have no idea what it thinks. You think it thinks nothing.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Go on to the next town. There is always one

effects.log: There is. You arrive in it with a bad cold and a lot of wrong ideas. People are not at all glad to see you. It is the most wonderful thing that has ever happened to anyone in your line.

choices.text: Go home once, to look, and do not stay

effects.log: The jar is being filled by somebody else. They do not know you. You lay your palm down on the old floor, when nobody is watching, and it is a good floor. You feel nothing. You take the morning cart, and you cry a little, and you could not say what about.

events.text: They have built a small roof over you, against the rain. You did not ask. People bring their disputes from the county town and sit in the yard to wait, and by the time you answer they have generally settled it. {npc} comes and tells you who has died. You mean to reply. There are some rather good beans on your left side. You have a sense of having got up to say something, a little while ago.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Answer, however late. They walked here

effects.log: It is about a boundary. It is a very good answer, it reaches them in nine years, and they have the grace to act surprised. Their grandchildren send a pig.

choices.text: Say nothing. You are holding up the county

effects.log: The county stands. They bring you new rice each autumn, with a straw cap, and they put it where you can see it. It has been some time since you felt your feet. You feel the feet of everybody else instead.

events.text: You wear clay in a cloth at your neck, you are sick on every road in the country, and you go anyway. They send for you when something is sinking: a dyke, a wall, a family. You come in late and grey, lie down on their floor, get up, and tell them which post. In the tenth month you are home with new rice. {npc} says it is a ridiculous way to live. {He} has saved you the good cushion.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Go out once more. There is a dyke at the ford

effects.log: It holds. They offer you silver, and you ask for a good dry floor for the night. You lie there thinking how bad it is, in great contentment, and you know the names of the people who will live on it.

choices.text: Stay home this year. Let the dyke wait

effects.log: It waits; dykes are patient, and most of them hold. You sit on your own floor all that winter, with your palm down, and you do not think about anything. It is exactly as good as you remembered, and by spring your feet have started to itch, which is new.

events.text: You can still get down to the floor. It is getting up that has become a matter for discussion. The young ones have made you a very fine raised bed with a carved rail, and they are hurt that you do not use it. {npc} says that you could at least get up on it for guests. "I will get to it," you say. You have always said that. Somebody else ties the jar knots now, and they are very neat.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Teach them to tie it badly

effects.log: It takes some doing. A knot should come loose, you tell them, when the rice wants to breathe. You have no idea if this is true. You only know that for you, nothing has ever felt right otherwise. They do it now, frowning, and {npc} covers {his} mouth.

choices.text: Get up on the bed, once, to keep the peace

effects.log: You lie up there for a whole evening, very stiff, looking at the rafters, with the guests. Everyone is so pleased. In the night you climb down again, which takes until dawn, and {npc} finds you there and says not a word.

events.text: They have asked where you want to be, at the end of it. The good room is ready, and it has a view. You have never cared for views. There is a discussion, and in the end four of them carry you to the middle of the old floor and set you down, with a good deal of fuss, on nothing. It is the tenth month. Someone in the yard is emptying the jar. {npc} sits down beside you, with some trouble.
events.arc: Blood of the Ground Under the House

choices.text: Put your palm down, and pat it twice

effects.log: You are not sure, afterwards, whether anything answered. You think that you may have to wait. You have time. {npc} puts {his} hand down next to yours, for company, though {he} says it is only for {his} back.

choices.text: Ask for the jar to be brought in, so that you can see the new rice

effects.log: They carry it in, grumbling. It is a good year. You put your hand in up to the wrist. It is cool, and slippery, and it smells of the whole of the valley. You leave your hand in there for some time, and no one likes to say anything.
